sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Ocean Vessel Freight and Wholesale Distribution of Hydraulic Cement

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (French-inspired code system with strong EU secondary-law overlay; no relevant sub-state divergence)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) — freedom of establishment and free movement of capital
EEA Agreement — access for EU/EEA counterparties

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: AML Law: Loi modifiée du 12 novembre 2004 relative à la lutte contre le blanchiment et le financement du terrorisme. UBO Register Law: Loi du 13 février 2018 relative au registre des bénéficiaires effectifs, as amended by Loi du 25 mars 2020 (transposition of EU Directive 2018/843). Commercial Companies Law: Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales. Supplementary rules: CSSF Regulation N° 12-02 and applicable EU Regulations on targeted financial sanctions.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation, memorandum and articles of association, and current register of directors of each corporate partner/shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry in the foreign partner's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (1961 Convention) or, for non-Apostille jurisdictions, consular legalization at the Luxembourg embassy/consulate; documents in non-supported languages must be accompanied by a sworn French/German/Luxembourgish translation.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized passport copy and proof of residential address for every natural-person beneficial owner, general partner (commandité), and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority or notary public in the individual's jurisdiction of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; the notarized copies must be dated no earlier than 90 days before submission.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original good-standing certificate and tax-residence certificate for each corporate partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Tax administration and/or companies registry of the corporate partner's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; where issued electronically, an apostilled PDF with a reliable electronic seal is acceptable under LBR practice.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney (procuration) appointing the Luxembourg notary and registered agent for the SCSp formation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The general partner(s) before a notary public in their jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; the original notarized instrument is retained by the Luxembourg notary and filed with the deed.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory baseline screening is performed against (i) UN Consolidated List, (ii) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions Database, (iii) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List for any USD or US-person touchpoint, and (iv) Luxembourg CSSF warnings and domestic anti-money-laundering watchlists. PEP exposure triggers enhanced due diligence under Article 3 of the Luxembourg AML Law as amended by EU Directive 2015/849: verified identity, source of wealth, source of funds, and senior-management approval. During the formation process, sanctions screening is repeated at least every 24 hours via a commercial screening tool; continuous risk-based monitoring applies post-incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — www.lbr.lu; Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via the e-RCS electronic filing portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official filing language for the RCS is French; German and Luxembourgish are also accepted for deeds. A company name may be in a foreign language, but if it is not in Latin script the RCS requires a Latin transliteration. The name must end with or include the legal-form suffix 'SCSp' or 'Société en Commandite Spéciale'; this suffix is compulsory and cannot be translated or omitted.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: An extension of the 30-day reservation may be requested through LBR before expiry only if a notarial appointment has been fixed; the registrar may grant a single 30-day extension. If the name is rejected, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the Luxembourg Ministry of Justice within 30 days and a judicial appeal before the Tribunal d'Arrondissement de Luxembourg (Commercial Chamber) within two months of notification. Alternatively, a fresh name may be submitted immediately for clearance; the rejected name remains blocked until the appeal is finally resolved.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office is permissible via a professional domiciliation company registered with the RCS, provided it maintains a physical address in Luxembourg and offers mail-forwarding, process-service, and administrative substance services. For the low-risk wholesale cement industry, no industry-specific physical-presence obligation applies; however, the SCSp must not constitute a letterbox arrangement for purposes of Luxembourg corporate-tax residence or anti-abuse rules.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; below 10% annual probability of a discretionary on-site inspection by the RCS or AML authorities for a non-regulated wholesale cement trader without sanctions exposure or UBO discrepancies. The probability rises above 35% if the entity is flagged in a suspicious transaction report, if an UBO is a PEP, or if shell indicators exist such as an identical registered address used by a large number of companies.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company name reservation and RCS non-confusion clearance
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory administrative tariff under the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 7 June 2001, as amended

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting, execution, and registration of the SCSp partnership deed (acte constitutif) and allied resolutions
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for a simple SCSp; notarial tariff for registration and annexed instruments

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille / consular legalization of foreign partner documents and GDPR-compliant certified translations
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Embassies, consulates, and sworn translation offices in partners' jurisdictions
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official consular fee schedule plus prevailing translation market rate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO identification and initial register filing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory filing charge per entity plus disclosed registered-agent fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office / commercial domiciliation agreement for twelve months
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Approved domiciliation service provider in Luxembourg
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Annual service contract benchmark for a low-risk commercial SCSp

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT customer due diligence, PEP and international sanctions screening, and internal compliance file
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed-fee engagement in line with prevailing counsel practice

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank pre-reference and account-opening introduction request (stage 1 preparatory only)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank tariff for account application, credit check, and KYC administration

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Articles 331-1 to 331-9 on Sociétés en Commandite Spéciale, introduced by Law of 12 July 2013)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte constitutif / Partnership Agreement (Contrat de Société) filed for RCS registration
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum capital requirement; SCSp has no legal personality; contributions are contractually determined and may be in cash, kind, or industry (only for general partners); no escrow account required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Unanimous Written Resolutions of the Founder (General Partner) of [Insert Name] SCSp, dated [Date]. The founder approves the adoption of the partnership agreement in the form annexed; subscribes to an initial partnership interest in the amount set forth in Schedule A, to be funded by wire transfer or in kind as stipulated; determines that the registered office shall be in Luxembourg City at [Address], Municipality of Luxembourg; and appoints [Name] as the initial managing partner (associé commandité) and [Name] as day-to-day manager (dirigeant), each with authority to open bank accounts, execute charter party agreements, sign commercial contracts, and represent the SCSp before the Luxembourg Business Registers, taxation authorities, customs, and any third parties. This resolution is effective upon signature.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and Execute the Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: All partners / notary public (if real estate contribution, notarial deed mandatory)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the SCSp partnership agreement (contrat de société) containing name, form, purpose, registered office address, capital contributions, profit-sharing rules, general and limited partners' rights and obligations, management powers, and dissolution terms. Ensure that the activity description is aligned with ISIC 4663 and the intended commercial model. Execute the agreement by all partners; if real estate is contributed, execute before a Luxembourg notary.
required_dossiers: Valid passport or ID of each partner
Proof of address of each partner
Draft partnership agreement
Ultimate beneficial ownership declaration for each partner (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS queries the partnership agreement due to incomplete or ambiguous clauses, file an addendum signed by all partners restating the missing details; pay any additional notarization fee if a notarial re-execution is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the electronic registration request via the LBR online portal (www.lbr.lu). Attach the signed partnership agreement, the UBO declaration, and the identification documents. Pay the registration fee via the portal (approximately EUR 50 + EUR 70 for the publication in the RESA). The RCS will issue the registration certificate once the file is complete and compliant.
required_dossiers: Signed partnership agreement (private deed or notarial copy)
UBO declaration form
Identification documents of partners and managers
Proof of registered office address in Luxembourg (lease or letter of  approval from domiciliation agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is placed on cure, respond to the RCS official comments within 15 days by correcting the submitted documents; if the deadline is missed, restart the filing with a new request and pay the fee again.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Electronic Companies and Associations Gazette (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Publication Department (Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, the RCS automatically transmits the key extracts (registration number, name, registered office, managers, object) to the RESA for publication. The publication is mandatory for third-party effect and is typically completed within 1-2 working days after registration. Monitor the publication reference and retain the RESA excerpt for banking and legal purposes.
required_dossiers: RCS registration number
Registration certificate (extract)
Notification of publication in RESA (issued automatically)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If no RESA publication appears within 5 business days, contact the LBR publication department with the RCS registration number and request expedited issuance; no additional fee is charged for correcting a missed publication.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain a VAT Number from the Luxembourg Indirect Tax Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for VAT registration using the RCS extract and the partnership's identification details. Submit the application through the MyGuichet.lu portal (form 640 – VAT initial registration). If the SCSp will conduct intra-Community acquisitions or exceed the local VAT registration threshold, VAT registration is mandatory. The AEDT will issue a Luxembourg VAT number upon successful review, typically within 10 business days.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate (extract)
Partnership agreement
Identification documents of the general partner
Description of planned activities and transaction flows
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the VAT application is rejected or since allegations of incomplete activity description, submit a revised activity description and reference to ISIC 4663 and the intended cross-border wholesale operations; re-apply via the online form with an explanatory note.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Corporate Bank Account and Complete Commercial Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial banks licensed in Luxembourg (CSSF regulated entities)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select a bank (e.g., any Luxembourg credit institution). Provide the RCS extract, partnership agreement, UBO identification, and a business plan describing the ocean vessel freight and wholesale distribution of Portland clinker. The bank will perform a KYC/KYT review. Upon account opening, execute the necessary account signatory mandates; this step completes the formational runway for operational trading.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate and RESA publication
Partnership agreement
Passports of partners and authorized signatories
UBO declaration
Business plan and forecast transaction volume
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional compliance information, supply audited or bank references from existing partners' banks; if the account is denied, approach a specialized private bank or a Luxembourg-based payment institution.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Luxembourg Ministry of the Economy (Ministère de l'Économie) – Directorate General for Industry and Commercial Establishment
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industry-specific operating license is mandated for pure ocean vessel freight and wholesale distribution of cement (ISIC 4663). A standard autorisation d'établissement may be required only if the SCSp opens a physical commercial or warehouse establishment in Luxembourg under the Law of 2 September 2011 on commercial establishment.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – No EIA required for wholesale/distribution without physical processing or manufacturing.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for pure trading and freight. If incidental warehousing of cement is established, compliance with the Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management and the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 10 July 2018 on air emissions will be referenced; safe dust containment and water runoff management are required in any future storage facility.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No fire safety certificate (certificat de sécurité incendie) or structural load inspection is required for an SCSp without physical premises. If an office or warehouse is later opened, a fire safety inspection by the Grand-Ducal Fire and Rescue Corps (CGDIS) and a workplace safety clearing per the Luxembourg Labour Code (Code du Travail) will be mandatory before the premises are used.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Luxembourg Inland Revenue (Administration des contributions directes, ACD) for income tax matters; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration. Centralized e-filing portal: MyGuichet.lu / eCDF (Electronic Customs and VAT Filing).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign investor establishing a Luxembourg SCSp must first obtain approval of the entity name and file incorporation documents with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) through a certified notary or fiduciary. Upon RCS registration, the SCSp automatically receives a Luxembourg 13-digit business identification number. For VAT and income tax purposes, the SCSp or its managing partner must file separate registration with the AEDT using the RCS number; non-EU resident partners acting as joint and several VAT representatives must indicate their status on the VAT registration form. If the SCSp makes taxable supplies, the AEDT issues a Luxembourg VAT number (numéro d'identification TVA) in addition to the national identification number.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No U.S.-style check-the-box election exists in Luxembourg. The SCSp is per se fiscally transparent, meaning profits and losses flow through to partners. Luxembourg law does not permit the SCSp to elect to be treated as a corporation for tax purposes. Binding advance tax rulings (conventions with the ACD) may be obtained to confirm the transparency of the SCSp, the treatment of hybrid instruments, and the allocation of income among partners, subject to the OECD/G20 Hybrid Mismatch rules as implemented in Luxembourg law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover (excluding VAT) for small businesses established in Luxembourg; no registration threshold applies to intra-Community acquisitions or imports of goods into Luxembourg.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control (CTC), or mandatory digital stamping regime is currently in force for domestic B2B transactions. E-invoicing is mandatory for suppliers to Luxembourg public sector entities, using the PEPPOL BIS Billing 3.0 format through the national Peppol access point. All VAT returns, recapitulative statements, and customs declarations must be filed electronically through the eCDF/MyGuichet platform; a dedicated e-invoice clearance and archiving environment for private contracts is not mandated.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods physically dispatched or transported to a destination outside the EU, including supplies of cement clinker loaded on ocean freight for non-EU buyers, qualify for the 0% VAT export rate provided the supplier retains full evidence of departure from the EU within the statutory time limit (normally 3 months following the supply). B2B services, such as commission-based international freight and wholesale logistics services, may be zero-rated or outside Luxembourg VAT when supplied to a non-EU business customer under the place-of-supply rules of Article 14 of Luxembourg VAT law. Exemptions are conditional on the export transaction being properly recorded in the exporter's books and supported by the consignee's valid non-EU VAT/GST registration number where applicable.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document - SAD/EX)
Export customs receipt or electronic export manifest (AES/ECS confirmation)
Bill of Lading (port-to-port ocean shipment) or other transport document (CMR/air waybill)
Commercial invoice (including shipment terms, Incoterms 2020, and export zero-rating annotation)
Packing list and weight certificate for bulk clinker cargo
Proof of physical transport to the non-EU destination (Port of loading / Port of destination evidence)
Supplier declaration / declaration of non-EU destination of goods
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or bank transfer confirmation evidencing receipt of export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT may audit zero-rated export transactions and require the full repayment (clawback) of any VAT claimed as zero-rated, together with interest at the legal rate, where the exporter fails to substantiate the physical exit of goods from the EU, lacks valid customs declarations, or does not provide credible evidence of payment and repatriation of foreign currency proceeds. Administrative penalties can reach 10% of the tax due for each incomplete accounting period, and VAT fraud penalties may be doubled or tripled depending on the intentional nature of the non-compliance; directors, managing partners, and appointed VAT representatives may be held jointly and severally liable. Criminal prosecution for deliberate export zero-rating fraud can lead to fines of EUR 250 to EUR 500,000 and imprisonment, as set out in the Luxembourg general tax law (Abgabenordnung) and VAT enforcement provisions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque Centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), the national central bank of Luxembourg and member of the Eurosystem, exercising monetary, macroprudential and payment-system oversight in coordination with the European Central Bank (ECB) and the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for supervised bank conduct.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full euro-area convertibility. The euro is fully convertible for the SCSp; there are no exchange-control permissions or surrender requirements for current-account or capital-account transactions. Article 63 TFEU and Directive 88/361/EEC guarantee free movement of capital, so partner equity injections, trade income, profit distributions and liquidation proceeds can be remitted freely without BCL/CSSF approval. The only mandatory compliance burden is the BCL balance-of-payments (BOP/IT) statistical declaration filed by the SCSp's bank, plus standard AML/KYC review. The tax-transparent status of the SCSp means profit distributions are partnership allocations rather than dividends; Luxembourg generally imposes no dividend withholding tax on such distributions to partners, provided the SCSp has not opted to be taxed as a corporate entity.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender, conversion ratio, or repatriation deadline exists in Luxembourg. Export and ocean-freight proceeds may be held freely in USD or EUR in onshore or offshore accounts without any mandatory exchange into euro. Where the SCSp clears proceeds through a Luxembourg bank, the credit is classified for BCL BOP/IT statistics as exports of goods or services, but no conversion or repatriation is imposed. Substance and transfer-pricing rules (OECD BEPS) still require that invoicing, booking and cash flows correspond to genuine commercial activity and that the SCSp maintains adequate economic substance in Luxembourg.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Epargne de l'Etat (Spuerkeess / BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW for offshore non-EU and third-country EMIs, which cannot passport into Luxembourg, lack SWIFT correspondent clearing capacity, and cannot issue documentary letters of credit. Feasibility rating: MEDIUM for CSSF-licensed Luxembourg payment institutions and e-money institutions, which may provide SEPA/instant payments, payment cards, and FX execution but are not substitutes for a Tier 1 bank account in high-value ocean-vessel bulk commodity settlement. For this SCSp (cement clinker bulk, USD/EUR wires, and LC), EMI rails are viable only as a secondary disbursement channel for low-value operating expenses; the primary clearing node must be a commercial bank with trade finance and correspondent banking relationships.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of the SCSp's General Partner (or an authorised managing director with power of attorney) and of each ultimate beneficial owner is the market standard for first-time onboarding. A physical compliance interview in Luxembourg, or at minimum a supervised videoconference, is generally required under the CSSF AML law of 12 November 2004 (as amended) and CSSF Circular 12/552. Remote-only opening is available at selected Tier 1 banks only where the group is already an established client, the UBO is an EU-resident professional, and certified/apostilled corporate documents, signature cards and notarised LPA are provided with e-signature support; otherwise the bank mandates an in-person or bank-visit interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque ultimate-beneficial-ownership chain in an SCSp contractual partnership without separate legal personality
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised Limited Partnership Agreement (LPA) with capital-account schedule; UBO declaration filed with the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); group organigram; passport, proof of address, and business rationale for each natural-person beneficial owner; explanation of the commercial role of each partner and the absence of nominee or custodial arrangements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Commodity trade red flags: possible fictitious, double-invoiced, or mis-described cement-clinker trades, or absence of physical cargo evidence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed sale and purchase contracts; pro-forma and commercial invoices with HS/CN code 2523.10 (Portland cement clinker); bills of lading and charter-party agreements; vessel name, IMO number and AIS track record of the ocean shipment; Incoterms; certificate of origin; weight and quality certificates; complete payment-chain documents matched to SWIFT MT103 references.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-wealth mismatch for a capital injection into a partnership with no statutory minimum capital
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Contribution resolution or subscription letter under the LPA; 12-month bank statements of the contributing partner; audited financial statements or notarised opening balance sheet; tax returns and tax-residency certificates; source-of-funds declaration; loan or escrow agreements where the contribution is pre-financed by a group treasury; demonstration that the injected amount is consistent with the stated trading plan for clinker procurement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or PEP exposure arising from shareholders, suppliers, or freight counterparties located in restricted or high-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: EU, UN, and OFAC sanctions screening reports for all counterparties, vessels, and beneficial owners; independent legal opinion on EU restrictive measures; corporate-register extracts and chamber-of-commerce verifications for suppliers; end-use and end-user certificates for the clinker cargo; verification that the cargo is destined for non-sanctioned EU or third-country ports; proof of vessel movement via AIS data.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: (i) the contributing partner instructs its bank to send an SWIFT MT103 credit to the SCSp account at the Luxembourg bank, quoting the SCSp name, BIC, and IBAN (EUR) or the corresponding USD account; (ii) the payment instruction must carry the ESP/EBA purpose code CAPT (capital payments) or TRDP (trade payments) and cite the LPA article governing capital contributions; (iii) the Luxembourg bank records the inward transfer under BCL BOP/IT statistics as a direct-investment capital contribution to a partnership; (iv) the credit is released only after AML/KYC verification of the remitter, the UBO chain, and the purpose; (v) no FX or exchange-control approval is required, but the credited funds must be matched against the signed contribution schedule and booked to the capital account to support future audits and bank transactions.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails: (a) SWIFT MT103 and MT202 COV wire transfers (telegraphic transfers) for advance payments, freight, port charges, storage, and open-account balances to suppliers; (b) commercial letters of credit (sight or usance) issued via SWIFT MT700 for bulk Portland clinker purchases, payable against a full set of negotiable bills of lading, commercial invoice, packing list, certificate of origin, and weight certificate; (c) standby or back-to-back letters of credit for supplier requests of first-demand guarantee security; (d) documentary collections (documents against payment or documents against acceptance) as a fallback. EUR settlements clear through TARGET2 via the Luxembourg bank; USD settlements clear through the bank's United States correspondent via Fedwire or CHIPS. Every outgoing instruction must reference the purchase-order number, LC number, and the commodity description 'cement clinker, CN 2523.10' to maintain consistency with customs, VAT, BOP, and AML documentation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD deliverable outright OTC forwards, non-cleared and EMIR margin-compliant, to lock conversion of USD trade receivables and ocean-freight income into EUR
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in EUR/TRY, EUR/EGP, and other restricted currencies applicable to clinker-supply corridors where onshore deliverability is limited
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD fixed-for-fixed or floating-for-fixed) for tenor-matched hedging of trade receivables, supplier payables, and vessel charter payment obligations
FX swaps combining spot and forward legs to manage short-term USD liquidity gaps in the SCSp's clearing account between letter-of-credit issuance and cargo collection dates

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (Comptes Annuels) - RCS Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS/LSC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 7 months after the close of the financial year (FYE 31 December => filing deadline 31 July); filing obligation applies even when the SCSp qualifies for the simplified small-company format
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal notice (mise en demeure) followed by court-ordered injunction at the entity's cost; criminal fine up to EUR 25,000; publication of the default; two consecutive years of non-filing triggers administrative strike-off (radiation) and judicial dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Registry of Beneficial Owners (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs, RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the anniversary of the initial RBE registration; any change in partnership interest ownership or control requires an interim update within 30 days of the transaction
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to EUR 1,250 per individual and EUR 5,000 per legal person for each violation; criminal imprisonment up to six months for repeated or fraudulent non-disclosure under the Law of 13 January 2019 as amended

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual RCS Data Currency Confirmation and Registered Office Re-verification
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS/LSC) via eRegistre/eFile portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuous statutory duty; annual verification cycle aligned with the UBO anniversary date; best practice requires confirming general partner (gérant), registered office, and partnership agreement details at each financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines under Article 22 of the Law of 19 December 2002; suspension of registration; risk of unenforceability of contracts and loss of third-party reliance on the official register

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit by an approved statutory auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé) when the SCSp exceeds at least two of the three following thresholds at the balance sheet date for two consecutive financial years: (i) balance sheet total > EUR 4.4 million (~USD 4.8 million); (ii) net turnover > EUR 8.8 million (~USD 9.5 million); (iii) average headcount > 50 employees. A contractual audit right granted to a partner or investor, or a lender covenant requiring certified accounts, independently triggers the audit mandate.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies as amended (accounting provisions of Article 68-1 et seq.); IFRS as adopted by the European Union is permitted for standalone financial statements; the SCSp's tax-transparent status does not relieve the entity of its statutory accounting and filing duties.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The general partner (associé gérant) must file and annually confirm all natural-person beneficial owners of the SCSp within 30 days after each anniversary of the initial RBE registration. Any transfer of partnership interests that alters proportionate ownership or control (relevant ownership threshold typically 25% or more direct/indirect, with any material change requiring immediate assessment) mandates an interim RBE update within 30 days of the transfer. The annual confirmation is completed online via the RBE portal; failure to confirm blocks issuance of the RBE certificate required for banking, financing, and counterparty due diligence.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Partners), Register of Directors (Gérant Resolutions), Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500 - USD 4,500 per annum for a licensed Luxembourg domiciliation agent including registered office, corporate secretarial support, and RCS correspondence handling
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 - USD 18,000 per annum for a certified statutory audit inclusive of Lux GAAP accounts preparation review; nil if the small-entity exemption applies, with a USD 2,000 - USD 5,000 accounting compilation alternative

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate statutory rate in Luxembourg-City, composed of 17% corporate income tax (CIT), a 7% solidarity surcharge on CIT, and a municipal business tax of 6.75%; non-city communes apply a municipal coefficient ranging from 6.75% to 11.28% (aggregate between 24.94% and ~29.47%).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced CIT of 15% on the first EUR 175,000 of taxable income; 80% net income exemption for qualifying IP (IP box); participation exemption on qualifying dividends and realized capital gains; 125% super-deduction for qualifying R&D expenses; investment tax credit for digital/energy transition investments.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 510 (declaration for the determination of taxable income of fiscally transparent partnerships / SCSp) filed electronically by the general partner through the ACD e-filing portal on MyGuichet.lu (LuxTrust authentication); a Form 420 (corporation tax return) is filed by each corporate partner resident in Luxembourg on its profit allocation.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending on 31 December, filing is due by 31 December of the following year; return preparers (accredited experts-comptables) benefit from an automatic extension to 30 April of the following year (in practice the ACD grants additional delay only upon request).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SCSp name, legal form code, RCS registration number, address, tax ID (matricule).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident general partner identifies itself and the appointed Luxembourg agent for service of process; non-resident limited partners are not listed individually.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax-adjusted book result: revenue, cost of goods sold, operating expenses, financial and extraordinary items, elimination of tax-exempt withholding items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All income from ocean-vessel freight and cement-clinker resale allocable to the Luxembourg commercial activity is reported in the Luxembourg income frame; foreign branch results are excluded unless attributable to a Luxembourg PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of the taxable result between partners according to the contribution and profit-sharing clauses of the SCSp agreement, stated per partner name, status (corporate/individual, resident/non-resident) and share percentage.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident partners without a Luxembourg PE, the allocation is reported as non-assessable in Luxembourg, subject to the absence of a Luxembourg permanent establishment; the form itself requires a statement of the PE analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of any Luxembourg source withholding tax (e.g., on dividends from portfolio, bank interest), foreign tax credits and the partner-level WHT at source.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners claiming treaty relief must attach the TRC and the ACD reduced-withholding forms before the distribution; the allocation itself is not subject to dividend WHT.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or omitted filing: immediate default assessment (taxation d'office) by the ACD; penalty of up to 10% of the assessed tax; interest at 0.6% per month (7.2% p.a.) on the unpaid balance; coercive fines up to EUR 25,000 under the Luxembourg General Tax Law; criminal exposure under the tax fraud provisions of the AO.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 420 (Luxembourg corporate income tax return) for each resident corporate partner of the SCSp; filed via e-file on MyGuichet.lu by the corporate partner, together with the municipal business tax declaration.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due by 31 December of the year following the fiscal year end (e.g., FY 2024 return due 31 December 2025); an accredited advisory extension is customarily accepted to 30 April.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer matricule, registered office, director details, place of effective management.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Not applicable: this Form 420 is filed by Luxembourg resident corporate partners; non-resident corporate partners without a Luxembourg PE file Form 410.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit computed on the basis of the commercial year, adjusted for non-deductible expenses and exempt participations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The allocated SCSp profit is reported gross of the transparency; the 80% IP exemption and participation exemption are applied on the partner level.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CIT base plus add-backs fixed by the municipal business tax code (including the 2% financing-expense add-back for certain debt-funded participations).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The municipal tax applies only where a Luxembourg resident corporate partner has a Luxembourg permanent establishment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Form 420: default assessment, 10% augmentation, monthly 0.6% interest; administrative fines up to EUR 25,000; criminal tax fraud proceedings in cases of intention.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% - an SCSp is fiscally transparent for Luxembourg income tax; payments of profit shares are partnership allocations and are not subject to the 15% Luxembourg dividend withholding tax applicable to joint-stock companies. A Luxembourg-resident corporate partner is taxed on the allocation as ordinary business income (subject to participation exemption where the SCSp interest qualifies under Art. 166 LIR).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: For a non-resident corporate partner with no Luxembourg PE: (1) obtain a TRC from the residence state; (2) execute an ACD beneficial-ownership and entity classification statement (SCSp transparency confirmation); (3) attach the statement to the annual declaration or to the paying agent before disbursement; (4) apply the applicable DTA provision (business profits, not dividends, because no distribution WHT is levied); (5) where an erroneous WHT has been made on a non-dividend allocation, file a reclaim with the ACD within the general 5-year limitation period, attaching the TRC and partnership agreement extracts.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: 0% Luxembourg WHT on interest paid by an SCSp to non-resident corporate lenders (no statutory interest WHT outside the financial-sector savings rules); Royalties: 10% statutory WHT on patent/copyright royalties paid to non-residents, reduced to 0%-5% under most treaties (e.g., 5% to non-residents under the US-Luxembourg treaty; 0% under EU Interest & Royalties Directive for qualifying EU associated companies), subject to TRC, beneficial ownership and substance.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 50,000,000 (Local File) for a Luxembourg entity with annual turnover above EUR 50 million; Master File and CbC Report required when the consolidated group revenue reaches EUR 750,000,000; below these thresholds, the taxpayer must still maintain contemporaneous arm's length documentation when undertaking intra-group transactions.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg has no standalone ESR statute as in the Caribbean model, but applies the OECD/ATAD general anti-abuse rule, the principal purpose test under tax treaties, and the ACD substance doctrine: an SCSp distributing cement clinker must demonstrate real presence (business plan, office or substance, personnel with decision-making authority, bank accounts, contractual records) in Luxembourg; a pure invoice-through entity with no substance will be challenged, possibly recharacterised as an artificial arrangement, and the zero-WHT/transparent treatment may be denied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully submitting false or incomplete SCSp or partner-level returns; deliberately understating cement trading margins, booking fictitious ocean-freight costs, or omitting sale invoices.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment from 2 months to 5 years (aggravated cases: up to 10 years) and fines up to EUR 250,000, plus automatic payment of the evaded tax, a 10% penalty and monthly 0.6% default interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner of the SCSp (and de facto managers) are jointly and severally liable for the evaded amounts, subject to seizure, travel bans, and personal surrender in extradition proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Artificial Shell/Substance Deficit (GAAR - Art. 6 AO / ATAD PPT)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a zero-substance SCSp purely as an offshore invoice and profit-shifting vehicle while all sales, procurement and shipping decisions are made abroad; no employees, no local decisions, no books in Luxembourg.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation and denial of transparency/participation exemption; retroactive reassessment of the entire profit at the 24.94% aggregate tax rate plus 10% penalty and 0.6% monthly interest; possible 5-year statute reopening for foreign-controlled entities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The ACD can pierce the veil if the entity is a sham; directors and the general partner are personally exposed for restitution of underpaid tax through the action en comblement du passif.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Buying clinker from a related supplier at inflated prices or selling to a related trader at a discount to shift profit abroad; TP documentation not prepared or pricing outside the tested TNMM arm's length range.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Upward adjustment of taxable profit in the SCSp and at partner level, disallowance of the corresponding cost, 10% surcharge, 0.6% monthly default interest, and penalty under the TP documentation rules; potential 5-year audit reopening.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the SCSp general partner may be liable for the adjusted tax if they knowingly signed the non-arm's-length intercompany agreements; criminal exposure where false invoices were used.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Beneficial Ownership Register and AML Breach
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file and keep updated the beneficial ownership declaration in the Luxembourg RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) within one month of any change; or conducting vessel-freight payments with undeclared beneficial owners or suspicious wire transfers without any CDD evidence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to EUR 250,000 and criminal fines up to EUR 1,250,000 for persistent non-disclosure; imprisonment up to 3 years for obstruction; freezing of bank accounts and prevention of profit repatriation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner and the compliance officer are personally liable for the register filings; the criminal sanctions apply directly to individual directors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Exercising day-to-day cement procurement, shipping contracts and re-sale negotiations from Luxembourg offices or personnel while booking all profit as foreign-source or as a foreign partner allocation, thereby concealing the Luxembourg PE of the non-resident partner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of the PE profit share at the 24.94% aggregate rate, plus the 10% penalty, 0.6% monthly interest and potential criminal sanctions for wilful concealment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The managing general partner who caused the concealment is personally jointly and severally liable; travel bans may be imposed during the criminal investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Illicit Dividends / Distributions From Insolvent SCSp
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing profits to limited partners without verifying the SCSp's solvency or without honoring preferential creditor claims (unpaid commercial creditors or tax debt).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of the distribution from the limited partners; directors' liability under Art. 59 of the Luxembourg Companies Law; criminal sanctions for abuse of creditors' rights.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner is presumed liable for the shortfall; a limited partner may lose its liability shield if it takes part in management; insolvency courts may issue personal contribution orders and travel bans.
